item.title: Inside the Outside–Coda
item.description: A question for AI: Suppose, having fed you the same set of facts, could you come up with a different conclusion or facts to support a different conclusion? The answer is revealing.

item.title: BUSINESS MONDAY: Spotlight on Domaney’s Liquors and Fine Wines in Great Barrington
item.description: Since 1973 (and for decades prior to that under another name), the family-owned and -operated enterprise has been a vital part of the community.

item.title: Southern Berkshire Regional School District in turmoil: Committee chair and vice chair apparently resign during meeting
item.description: A complaint over the treatment of Superintendent Brian Ricca set off a chain of events that ended with the apparent resignations of the Southern Berkshire Regional School District Committee's chair and vice chair.

item.title: ‘Hadestown: Teen Edition’—March 12 through 15 at Monument Mountain Regional High School
item.description: “'Hadestown' asks big questions about fear, power, climate, economic struggle, and what happens when people lose hope, and those themes feel incredibly relevant today,” says director Josh Williams. But what makes the show truly powerful in his opinion is how relatable the characters are.

item.title: Pittsfield Cultural Council announces 48 grant awards for 2026
item.description: Through funding provided by the Massachusetts Cultural Council (MCC), the PCC is supporting 48 projects that span a wide range of disciplines, including visual arts, music, theater, dance, literature, and community events.

item.title: The 90 percent solution: Lowering taxes for year-round residents
item.description: There is no universal fix to help all of our challenges, but one instrument the state has given towns to sustain and stabilize their full-time population is the residential tax exemption.

item.title: PREVIEW: West Stockbridge Chamber Players winter concert on Sunday, March 15
item.description: The benefit concert at Old Town Hall features works by Enescu, Penderecki, Dohnányi, and Mozart.

item.title: THEATER REVIEW: ‘Dear Jack, Dear Louise’ plays at the Majestic Theater through April 4
item.description: I liked the play three years ago at Shakespeare & Company when Ariel Bock directed it, but I liked it even more under Dziura’s vision. I highly recommend this show. I would see it again.

item.title: PETER MOST: Avoiding the fiscal death spiral
item.description: What follows are some ideas raised around the table at Rubi’s, other ideas that deserve consideration, and at least one wisely rejected.

item.title: BITS & BYTES: Artemis at The Clark; Close Encounters With Music at The Mahaiwe; ‘The Mission’ at Linde Center; Cornelia Brooke Gilder at Ventfort Hall; Christa Joy & The Honeybees at Hot Plate; Beyond The Wall at The Colonial
item.description: The performance promises to be filled with joy, passion, and high-wire intensity.
